quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone died, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 damage to government property like signs).

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly at all times when you drive.

questions.question: What safety devices work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chances of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury by more than half. Airbags with safety belts provide extra protection in front crashes. Always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle immediately. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary, but apply pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency workers to arrive.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.
questions.explanation: Take a break every hour on long trips to avoid tiredness. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in the direction of the arrow, prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is near.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive with care, and watch for children.

questions.question: The driver ahead is using one hand to drive and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Stay farther back from their vehicle.
Know they are not paying full attention to driving.
Do not drive like they do.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for items, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. If another driver seems distracted, stay farther back because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and pass many vehicles, what will happen?

options.text: You will arrive faster and more safely.
You will increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Every time you pass a vehicle, your risk of a crash increases.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When a school bus has flashing lights.

questions.explanation: Never pass if there is oncoming traffic, your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, near a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no-passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a multilane road with a median or shared center turn lane.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, lowers your awareness, and harms your judgment — just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: You see people walking near the road. You should:
questions.explanation: Watch for people who may walk into your path. If you see people near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When you reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait until the tracks are clear, then go when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait until the tracks are clear, then go when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers show a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: A shiny orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:
questions.explanation: A shiny orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it is traveling slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.

questions.explanation: Don't make a last-minute turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, go to the next one.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull over and back up to the exit.
Stop a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop on the highway, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the only way to reduce the effects is by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers will not speed this up. One drink takes about one hour to leave your system.

questions.question: A green arrow on a lane control signal means:

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must move to this lane.

questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid when turning. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?

options.text: Wait for your body to process it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process it.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your blood alcohol level. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not work. You must wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection. A crosswalk exists at any intersection, whether it is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross after the "Don't Walk" signal begins to flash. The pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian in the intersection cross first. Wait until the pedestrian has completely crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, you must stop your vehicle before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, make a complete stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Use your turn signal to alert other drivers.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before making any side-to-side movement.
